chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from Muawiyah ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

One who recites the Surahs 'Abasa', 'Takwir', and 'Infitar' will be under the wing of Allah among the gardens of Paradise, and in the shade of Allah and His honor within His gardens, and it will not be great for Allah, if Allah wills.

key_terms.تَحْتَ جَنَاحِ اللَّهِ: Under the wing of Allah (divine protection)
key_terms.وَإِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ: And when the sun is wrapped up (folded), Quran Chapter 81
key_terms.وَتَوَلَّى: And Takwir (The Folding Up), Quran Chapter 81
key_terms.وَلَا يَعْظُمُ ذَلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ: And it is not difficult/great for Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Abasa, Takwir, and Infitar?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to emphasize the immense spiritual merit of reciting Surahs 'Abasa, 'Takwir', and 'Infitar', linking their themes of divine accountability to the promise of being sheltered under Allah’s wings in Paradise. This reward signifies not only entry into Jannah but also a state of intimate divine favor and honor, reflecting the Shia tradition of valuing specific recitations for their intercessory and protective qualities.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan from Muawiyah b. Wahab from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

“One who recites Surah Abas and Takrim would remain under the shade of Allah and would remain safe from usurping others’ property. He would receive favor of Allah and go to Paradise. And it is not a big thing for Almighty Allah.”
